title: I Challenged 3 Strangers to Make $1 With AI: Lessons From Three First Dollars
summary: Rob Hallam recaps a 6-week challenge where three first-time builders got a $100 budget and one goal: build with AI and earn their first dollar. All three did, via different routes: steady progress around a 9-to-5, a pivot after no one bought, and value-first cold outreach. Rob's takeaways are persistence, listening to users, and treating the first dollar as a beginning.

principles.text: Your first idea often fails; listen to your market, set your ego aside and pivot.
principles.quote: if you listen to your market and you speak to the users that you are trying to sell to, and you understand what exactly their problems are, and you're willing to set your ego aside and pivot your product

principles.text: Stated interest is not demand; paying customers are the real signal.
principles.quote: They might say they want it, but they're not putting their money where their mouth is.

principles.text: Progress comes from small consistent steps, not one big leap.
principles.quote: getting what you want out of life literally consists of taking one step at a time, putting one foot in front of the other.

principles.text: Painful, manual outreach is often what produces the first sale.
principles.quote: grinded through the 50 DMs to make his first sale, even if it was painful

principles.text: Open sales conversations by giving value first, starting with finding the right leads.
principles.quote: Everything from finding the leads to opening up with giving them value, right?

principles.text: Start, ship, sell and keep going through rejection; the first dollar is a beginning.
principles.quote: They started. They shipped something. And they sold it. They got rejected several times for some of them. But they kept going.
